items.originalTitle: George Russell calls for F1 track changes after Max Verstappen's COTA complaints
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔呼吁F1赛道改进
乔治·拉塞尔在马克斯·维斯塔潘对美洲赛车场的批评后，呼吁F1赛道每隔几年进行翻新。
对于梅赛德斯车队的粉丝来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃斯的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析。
乔治·拉塞尔在马克斯·维斯塔潘对美洲赛车场的路面坑洼提出批评后，呼吁F1赛道每隔几年进行翻新。他认为这可能导致维斯塔潘需要‘新的脊椎’。
COTA长期以来一直被认为是一级方程式赛历上最颠簸的赛道之一。但这位荷兰人看到赛车和车手在赛道举行的耐力锦标赛上的表现时感到震惊。
“但这是一条非常不同的赛道，”他说。“从我参加的WEC来看，赛道非常颠簸。哦我的天，我可能需要在周末之后订购一个新的脊椎，或者变成像机器人警察那样。太疯狂了。”
在周四的媒体会上被问及这个问题时，这位梅赛德斯车手同意赛道很颠簸，但他表示问题不仅仅局限于COTA。老化的沥青已经影响了24站赛历中的多个赛道。
“是的，很颠簸，但我认为这只是赛车的一部分，”他说。“我认为我的总体观点是一级方程式赛道可能需要每两年重新铺设一次，以便使其更加一致，因为我们现在去到的赛道上，沥青正在脱落，正在破碎，它造成的问题比解决的问题还要多。
“我们不是那种Indy赛车或F2赛车，它们的行驶高度相对较高，我们的行驶高度在直道结束时是10毫米，离地面只有一厘米，所以任何微小的颠簸你都能真切地感觉到。”
在摩纳哥大奖赛上，拉塞尔·斯特罗尔和查尔斯·勒克莱尔都在第19弯道发生碰撞，比赛因FIA检查赛道表面而红旗暂停。两位车手都指责他们的赛车存在问题，但许多人将事故与受损的沥青路面联系起来。
“自从我们换上了18英寸轮胎后，轮胎的侧面轮廓现在明显更小，”拉塞尔继续说。“轮胎的周长相同，但轮圈的周长要大得多，所以你在轮胎上失去了所有的有效悬挂，那是一个减震器，我们现在似乎已经没有了。所以，再次强调，这不是理想的情况，但我们能做的并不多。”
拉塞尔以车手锦标赛第二名的身份抵达奥斯汀，落后于队友基米·安东内利102分，理论上他可以在本周日赢得车手总冠军。本周末，两位梅赛德斯车手都将使用车队最新的升级套件，拉塞尔表示，这些新部件需要“比我们最初预期的更大的设置调整”。
detailEn: George Russell calls for F1 track changes after Max Verstappen's COTA complaints
George Russell believes Formula 1 circuits should be resurfaced every couple of years
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

George Russell believes Formula 1 circuits should be resurfaced every couple of years after Max Verstappen made critical comments about the bumps at the Circuit of the Americas and how they could leave him needing “a new spine”.

COTA has for a long time been known as one of the bumpier circuits on the Formula 1 calendar. But the Dutchman was alarmed when he saw what the cars and drivers went through during the World Endurance Championship race at the circuit.

“But it’s again a very different track," he said. "From what I saw in WEC, the track is incredibly bumpy. Oh my God, I probably need to order a new spine after the weekend, or become like Robocop. Crazy.”

Asked about the issue during his media session on Thursday in Austin, the Mercedes driver agreed the track is bumpy, but said the problem isn't just limited to COTA. Ageing asphalt has affected several circuits across the 24-race calendar.

“Yeah, it’s bumpy, but I think it’s just part of racing," he said. "I’d say my general view is F1 tracks probably need to be repaved every couple of years just to make it a bit more consistent, because we’re going to tracks now where tarmac’s coming up, it’s falling apart, it’s causing more issues than not.
"We’re not an Indy car or an F2 car that run their ride heights reasonably high, our ride height’s 10mm at the end of the straight, a centimetre from the ground, so any tiny bump you really feel it.”

At the Monaco Grand Prix, Lance Stroll and Charles Leclerc both crashed at Turn 19, and the race was red-flagged while the FIA inspected the track surface. Both drivers blamed problems with their cars, but many linked the incidents to the damaged asphalt.

“The side profile of the tyres now since we’ve been at the 18-inch is substantially smaller," Russell continued. "The circumference of the tyre is the same, the circumference of the rim is far greater, so you’ve lost all of that effective suspension in the tyre, which was a damper, which we kind of don’t have anymore. So, again, not ideal, but not much we can do.”

Russell arrives in Austin second in the drivers’ championship, 102 points behind Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who can theoretically win the drivers' championship this Sunday. Both Mercedes drivers will run the team’s latest upgrade package this weekend, with Russell saying the new parts need “a bigger set-up adjustment than we first anticipated”.

items.titleZh: 梅赛德斯推迟ADUO引擎首秀
items.summaryZh: 梅赛德斯升级的F1引擎不会像最初预期的那样在美国大奖赛上亮相。由于梅赛德斯被认为比基准2026动力单元（红牛）落后超过2%，因此它可以引入中期升级。
items.originalTitle: Mercedes rolls back ADUO engine debut
detailZh: 梅赛德斯升级的F1引擎不会像最初预期的那样在美国大奖赛上亮相。
梅赛德斯被认为比基准2026动力单元（红牛）落后超过2%，由F1的额外开发和升级机会（ADUO）系统判定，这意味着它可以引入中期升级。
原计划在本周末奥斯汀引入升级，但因动力单元未准备好而推迟。
《The Race》了解，它也不会在下周末的墨西哥大奖赛准备好，这意味着F1最新三连赛的最后一站巴西大奖赛很可能是它最早到达的日期。
乔治·拉塞尔在本月伊始在雪邦遭遇的引擎故障对他来说是个打击，因为这意味着他在新加坡需要接受发车线处罚。
每次他使用ADUO梅赛德斯引擎时，他都必须接受另一个发车线处罚。
梅赛德斯只有在确信这是真正的一大步时，才会引入ADUO引擎。
车队几乎肯定将赢得2026年的两项冠军，但任何在2026年底引入的赛车和引擎升级都将对2027年产生重大影响。
所以，无论梅赛德斯在其ADUO引擎上能取得多少进步——即使它只用于2026年两三个周末——对下一年来说都可能非常有用。
梅赛德斯将在奥斯汀使用它在雪邦首次亮相的主要底盘升级，因为它在上次新加坡的比赛中采取了不同寻常的方法，将规格分给了两辆赛车。
那次实验在新加坡周末期间让梅赛德斯学到了很多，而自那以后团队完成的简报又给了它更多关于如何最好地利用升级的线索。
两位车手将从FP1开始就拥有升级后的赛车。
detailEn: Mercedes’ upgraded Formula 1 engine won’t appear as initially expected at the United States Grand Prix.

Mercedes was deemed to be more than 2% adrift of the benchmark 2026 power unit (Red Bull) by F1’s Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system, meaning it can introduce a mid-season upgrade.
That upgrade was initially pencilled in for introduction at Austin this weekend, but that plan has been pushed back because the upgraded power unit isn’t ready.

The Race understands it won’t be ready for next weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix either, meaning the Brazilian Grand Prix that concludes F1’s latest triple-header is the likely earliest date it will arrive.
George Russell’s engine failure at Sepang at the start of this month was a blow for him as it meant he had to take a grid penalty in Singapore.
He’ll have to take another grid penalty whenever he takes the ADUO Mercedes engine.
Mercedes only wants to introduce the ADUO engine when it’s convinced it’s a proper step forward.
The team’s all but certain to win both 2026 titles, but any car and engine upgrades introduced in late-2026 will have a significant impact on 2027.
So whatever progress Mercedes can make with its ADUO engine - even if it’s only used in two or three 2026 weekends - could be very useful for next year.
Mercedes is going to run the major chassis upgrade it debuted at Sepang on both cars at Austin, having taken the unusual route of splitting specification between its cars last time out in Singapore.
That experiment taught Mercedes plenty during the Singapore weekend, and the debriefs the team has completed since that weekend have given it further clues as to how best to exploit the upgrade.
Both drivers will have the upgraded car right from FP1.
keyPointsZh: 原计划在本周末奥斯汀引入升级，但因动力单元未准备好而推迟
keyPointsEn: The upgrade was initially scheduled for this weekend in Austin, but has been postponed due to the unavailability of the upgraded power unit

items.originalTitle: Lando Norris backs Max Verstappen over COTA bumps, reveals headache tablet use
detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯支持维斯塔潘对COTA的批评，透露在驾驶前服用头痛药片
兰多·诺里斯支持维斯塔潘对美洲赛车场的批评，透露一些一级方程式赛道的坑洼如此严重，以至于他在驾驶前需要服用头痛药片
对于麦凯轮车迷来说，来自沃金克的木瓜新闻，包括关于车手、赛车、团队策略以及每个周末的比赛的最新消息
兰多·诺里斯支持维斯塔潘，他表示一些一级方程式赛道，包括美洲赛车场的坑洼非常严重，以至于他在开始驾驶前需要服用头痛药片
在观看了COTA的世界耐力锦标赛比赛后，维斯塔潘开玩笑说，他周末可能需要订购一个新的脊椎，或者变成像《银翼杀手》中的机器人警察。在奥斯汀比赛前的周四，这位荷兰人越来越批评赛道。当诺里斯不久后被问及此事时，他支持了他对手的观点。
“嗯，我会说是的。我的意思是，如果你现在建造一条新的赛道，FIA……建造新赛道的规则，你必须遵守的公差非常小。它肯定不符合现在的这些规定，让我们说，但这是一条旧赛道，不是一条新赛道——它真的很糟糕。”
他进一步解释了这有多么困难。
“有很多地方我出门前需要吃头痛药。仅仅是因为它太颠簸了，你因为颠簸而重重地撞在头枕上，所以这绝对不是一件愉快的事情。”
“但我们能做的并不多。我的意思是，我们对此抱怨，所以这确实被提了很多次，但我们能抱怨的事情有限，但他是对的。当然是对的。”
COTA的赛道表面自从2012年F1首次在那里比赛以来一直是一个长期存在的问题。在2023年在奥斯汀获胜后，维斯塔潘表示，这些凹凸不平的地方“不符合F1标准”，赛道主席鲍比·爱泼斯坦当时承诺要修复最严重的地方。2024年，整个赛道都进行了翻新，今年也进行了工作，以修复9号弯和11号弯之间的最严重问题。
梅赛德斯车队的乔治·拉塞尔也谈到了奥斯汀的凹凸不平，称其为“赛车的一部分”，但认为F1赛道应该“每隔几年”就翻新一次。他说，在直道结束时，赛车离地面只有10毫米，而18英寸轮胎较小的侧壁意味着车手能感觉到每一个凹凸。
F1与COTA签订了直到2034年的比赛合同，这是在去年达成新协议后确定的。
detailEn: Lando Norris backs Max Verstappen over COTA bumps, reveals headache tablet use
Lando Norris has backed Max Verstappen's criticism of the Circuit of the Americas, revealing that bumps at some Formula 1 tracks are so severe he takes headache tablets before driving
For McLaren fans. Papaya news from Woking, with the latest on the drivers, the car, team strategy and every race weekend.
Lando Norris has backed Max Verstappen as he says the bumps at some Formula 1 circuits, including the Circuit of the Americas, are so bad that he takes headache tablets before he starts driving.

Having watched the World Endurance Championship race at COTA, Verstappen joked that he would "need to order a new spine after the weekend, or become like Robocop". On the Thursday ahead of the Austin race, the Dutchman was increasingly critical of the track. When Norris was asked shortly after, he supported his rival's opinion.

“Well, I would say yes. I mean, if you build a new track now the FIA... the rules, the regulation of building a new track, the tolerances you have to be within are pretty small. It certainly doesn’t fit anywhere close to what those regulations are now, let’s say, but it’s an old track, not a new track - it’s pretty bad.”
He explained further just how difficult it can be.

“There’s a lot of places I need to take headache tablets before I go out. Simply because it’s so bumpy and you're hitting your head pretty hard against the headrests and things because of the bumps, so it’s certainly not a nice thing.
"But there's not much we can do. I mean we complain about it, so it’s certainly brought up many, many times but there’s only so much we can complain about things, but he’s right. Certainly right.”

COTA’s surface has been a long-running issue since F1 first raced there in 2012. After winning in Austin in 2023, Verstappen said the bumps were “not F1 level”, and circuit chairman Bobby Epstein promised at the time to fix the worst areas. In 2024, the whole track was resurfaced, and work has been done this year to remedy the worst of it between Turn 9 and Turn 11.

Mercedes’ George Russell also spoke about the bumps in Austin, calling them “part of racing” but arguing that F1 tracks should be resurfaced “every couple of years”. He said the cars run just 10mm off the ground at the end of the straights, and that the smaller sidewalls of the 18-inch tyres mean drivers feel every bump.
F1 has a contract to race at COTA until 2034, after a new deal was agreed last year.

keyPointsEn: Max Verstappen takes headache tablets after the race at COTA

梅赛德斯一级方程式车手乔治·拉塞尔已经回应了前红牛车队首席执行官兼车队总监克里斯蒂安·霍纳的指控，称他、兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里曾作为青训车手付费使用红牛的模拟器
霍纳，去年被红牛车队解雇，本周在《高性能播客》中说，这三名车手在年轻的时候都支付了使用车队模拟器的费用。据霍纳所说，管理模拟器的人告诉他，这三名年轻车手比红牛已有的车手更好，但赫尔穆特·马克罗对签下他们不感兴趣。
“我记得乔治·拉塞尔在支付我们使用模拟器，兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里也是如此。他们的父亲在给他们开支票，让他们在我们的驾驶员模拟器上运行，”霍纳说。
“负责这个的人走过来对我说，‘克里斯蒂安，这些孩子比我们目前有的青训车队车手更好。’我记得把他们带到赫尔穆特面前，说，‘看，我真的认为你应该看看这些家伙。’”
目前位列车手锦标赛第二位的拉塞尔在美国大奖赛前的媒体采访中被问到了霍纳的评论。
“所以回到2013年，模拟器对任何人来说都不是什么常见的东西，”这位英国车手解释道。“当时的青训车队没有模拟器，有机会在Formula Renault赛车上的模拟器里进行一些驾驶练习，所以这更多的是为了测试和为我们在参加的系列赛中驾驶做准备，因为正如我所说的，没有车队拥有它。这就是全部了。我就说这么多。”
美国大奖赛定于10月23日至25日在美国赛车场举行，并开启了赛季倒数第二个三连赛。
detailEn: George Russell responds to Christian Horner's Red Bull simulator claim
George Russell has responded to Christian Horner's claims that he, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri paid to use Red Bull's simulator as junior drivers
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has responded to former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner's claims that he, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri used to pay to use the Milton Keynes outfit's simulators.

Horner, who was dismissed from Red Bull last year, said on the High Performance podcast this week that all three drivers had paid to use the team's simulator when they were younger. According to Horner, the person running the simulator told him the three young drivers were better than those Red Bull already had, but Helmut Marko was not interested in signing them.

"I remember George Russell was paying us to go on our simulator, as was Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Their dads were writing cheques for them to run on the driver simulator that we had," Horner said.

"And the guy that was looking after it was coming up to me and saying, 'Christian, these kids are better than the juniors we've got at the moment.' I remember taking them to Helmut and going, 'Look, I really think you should look at these guys.'"
Russell, who currently sits second in the drivers' championship, was asked about Horner's comments while speaking to the media ahead of the United States Grand Prix.

"So back in 2013, simulators weren't really a thing for anybody," the British driver explained. "Any junior teams didn't have simulators and there was an opportunity to do some driving on that simulator in the Formula Renault car, so it was more as preparation for testing and driving for the series that we were racing because, as I said, no teams had it. So that's the extent of it. That's all I'll say."
The United States Grand Prix is scheduled for 23-25 October at the Circuit of the Americas and kicks off the penultimate triple-header of the season.

items.titleZh: 维斯塔潘担心美国赛车场事故导致更多脊椎损伤
items.summaryZh: 维斯塔潘担心如果不对美国赛车场的失控碰撞采取行动，F1车手将遭受比近年来更多的脊椎损伤。
items.originalTitle: Verstappen’s spinal damage fears from ‘out of control’ F1 bumps
detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘担心，如果像美洲赛车场那样的“失控”碰撞问题得不到解决，一级方程式车手将遭受比近年来已经遭受的“更多”的脊椎损伤。
奥斯汀赛道的崎岖不平已经让一级方程式车手和他们的MotoGP同行们多年来感到沮丧，2022年的一项重大翻新计划旨在缓解最严重的投诉。
在今年的一级方程式比赛之前，赛道再次进行了翻新，从第9个弯道入口到第11个弯道入口，并在第12个和第19个弯道入口进行了平整，以消除凸起。
但四次一级方程式世界冠军维斯塔潘——他说，上个月世界耐力锦标赛在那里比赛时，它仍然看起来“极其崎岖”——认为这些只是表面的改进。
他建议，如果需要一个大型的土方工程来加固地表下移动的地面和土壤，那么COTA应该负责这项工作——即使这是一项漫长的任务。
“你可以用土壤问题是借口，但你应该知道这一点，你需要确保你加固它更多，”他说。
“我的意思是，我热爱这条赛道，我热爱这个地方。这是有史以来最好的布局之一。这也是最好的场馆，最好的城市之一。但对我来说，我们有的颠簸是不可接受的。
“随着时间的推移，他们在这里那里磨了一点，但这只是在给大问题贴上膏药。这就是下面的问题所在。这就是你首先需要解决的问题。”
“但是这意味着你需要真正完全地打开赛道。这需要花费大量的金钱和时间。但说实话，这是唯一能够解决这个问题的方式，因为这些凸起不是自然的，而且它们失去了控制。”
虽然维斯塔潘认为这条赛道是一个极端的例子，但他建议这是一个F1需要更加认真对待的更广泛的问题。
COTA赛道上最颠簸的部分，包括在长长的直道末端，都位于减速区进入慢弯道，维斯塔潘表示这实际上使得当前的车对于驾驶员的不适感比地面效应的前辈车型更甚。
在2022-2025规则集早期，车手们抱怨那些硬朗、低矮的赛车有多么不舒服——尤其是在直道上。
当前赛车在弯道中的实际行驶高度更低，当前后翼关闭且车辆因下压力重新附着而降低速度时，车辆会非常积极地触底进入制动区域。
去年，你在弯道中能产生大约5-6G的加速度，但我有一些垂直载荷的冲击，这就像我的脊椎上超过9G的加速度，我可以告诉你这真的很不舒服，”维斯塔潘说。
而且随着年龄的增长，你越会更多地考虑这一点。
我可以告诉你，从我脊椎的检查来看，底部的情况看起来并不太好。
“我知道那也是赛车的一部分，那也可以是体育的一部分，但它也是对我们过去几年所拥有的赛车造成的进一步损害，现在如果我们继续认为驾驶在这样的赛道上是可以接受的，你将承受更多的痛苦。”
“人们可以说，确实有比这更糟的体育项目会对你的身体部位造成伤害，但这就是为什么我不做这些项目的原因！”
维斯塔潘也在这个话题上与对手乔治·拉塞尔和兰多·诺里斯找到了共同点。
拉塞尔建议一级方程式赛道应该“每隔几年重铺一次……因为我们现在去的是沥青正在冒出来、正在破碎的赛道，这会引起问题。”
“我们不是一辆像Indycar或F2那样行驶高度相对较高的赛车。我们的行驶高度在直道结束时是10毫米。所以任何微小的颠簸，你都能真切地感觉到，”他补充道。
“而且，自从我们使用了18英寸轮胎以来，轮胎的侧面轮廓也大大减小了。所以你失去了轮胎中所有的有效悬挂，这相当于我们不再拥有的阻尼器。”
现任冠军诺里斯表示，新赛道现在所需的公差“相当小”，并建议COTA“肯定不符合现在的那些规定”。
“情况相当糟糕，”他说。“有很多地方我需要出去前吃头痛药，仅仅是因为路面太颠簸，而且因为颠簸，你的头会重重地撞在头枕上和其他东西上。”
“这当然不是一件好事。但我们能做的并不多。我们对此抱怨，所以这是我们多次提出的问题，但我们能抱怨的也只有这么多。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen fears that Formula 1 drivers will suffer “much more” spinal damage than what they have already sustained in recent years if “out of control” bumps like those at the Circuit of the Americas are not addressed.

The bumpy nature of the Austin track has been a frustration for F1 drivers and their MotoGP counterparts for many years, with a major resurfacing initiative in 2022 aimed at alleviating the worst of the complaints.
It has also been resurfaced again ahead of this year’s F1 race, from the entry of Turn 9 to the entry of Turn 11, and smoothed at the entry of Turns 12 and 19, to remove bumps.

But four-time F1 world champion Verstappen - who said it still looked “extremely badly bumpy” when the World Endurance Championship raced there last month - believes these are superficial improvements.
He suggested that if a major earthworks project is required to reinforce the shifting ground and soil beneath the surface, then COTA should do it - even if it is a lengthy undertaking.
“You can use the excuse that the soil is the problem, but then you should have known that and you need to make sure that you reinforce it more,” he said.
“I mean, I love this track, I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever. And it's one of the best venues, best cities to be at. But for me, the bumps that we have are unacceptable.

“Over time they've been grinding a little bit here and there, but it's just you're putting a plaster on the big problem. And that's just what's coming underneath. That's what you need to actually tackle in the first place.

“But that means you need to really fully open up the track. That costs a lot of money and time. But honestly, that's the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural and they are out of control.”
While Verstappen believes this track is an extreme example, he suggested it is a wider issue that F1 needs to take more seriously.

Several of the COTA track’s bumpiest parts, including at the end of the long back straight, are in braking zones into slow corners which Verstappen said actually makes the current cars worse for driver discomfort than the ground-effect predecessors.
Early in the 2022-2025 ruleset drivers complained about how uncomfortable those stiff, low cars were - particularly on the straights.

The current cars actually run at lower ride heights in the corners, though, and can bottom out aggressively into braking zones when the front and rear wings close and car hunkers down as the downforce reattaches and speed drops off.
“Last year, you pulled around 5-6G in a corner, but I had some impacts like vertical load, which was like over 9G on my spine, which I can tell you is really not fun,” Verstappen said.
“And especially the older you get you think about that more and more.
“I can tell you from the checks that I’ve done from my spine, the bottom end doesn’t look that great.

“I know that’s part of racing, that can be part of sport, but it’s also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years, and now if we continue finding this acceptable to drive on you are going to suffer with that much more.
“And people can say there are worse sports out there for damage to parts of your body for sure, but that’s why I’m not doing them!”
Verstappen found some common ground with rivals George Russell and Lando Norris on this subject, too.
Russell suggested F1 tracks should be “repaved every couple of years…because we're going to tracks now where tarmac's coming up, it's falling apart” and causing issues.
“We're not an Indycar or an F2 car that runs ride heights reasonably high. Our ride height is 10mm at the end of the straight. So any tiny bump, you really feel it," he added.

“And the side profile of the tyres, since we've been with the 18 inch, is substantially smaller. So you've lost all of that effective suspension in the tyre, which was a damper we kind of don't have anymore.”
Reigning champion Norris said the tolerances new circuits need to be within now “are pretty small” and suggested COTA “certainly doesn't fit anywhere close to what those regulations are now”.

"It's pretty bad," he said. "There's a lot of places I need to take headache tablets before I go out, simply because it's so bumpy and you're hitting your head pretty hard against the headrest and things because of the bumps.
"So it's certainly not a nice thing. But there's not much we can do. We complain about it, so it's stuff we've brought up many, many times but there's only so much we can complain about."
